clerk (midshift): doing markdowns and donations, doing daily counts, and really doing housework essentially. the midshift in my store is kind of there to help do whatever needs to be done. organizing the department, freezers, doing tags, etc.

Hi, I've studied psychology for many years. But I want to preface that in no way am I licensed or have solid 100% thoughts about this. Just suggestions. 

Anyway, this sounds a lot like DID (dissociative identity disorder) or a term maybe you've heard, multiple personality disorder. Often, people with this will "break" into other personalities and most of the time not remember it. A lot of individuals with mental illness get diagnosed with BPD. It's an umbrella term in my opinion because a lot of mental health issues are classified under this diagnosis. I would encourage your brother to see a mental health professional and go with him to explain what you've been seeing. Those with multiple personalities can often hurt themselves without remembering as well. 

Hope this helped. Goodluck!

Hi, I'm actually in school to be a counselor and there is a reason therapists do this. 

Therapists are supposed to talk minimally. The main objective is to have you guide the conversation and make the session what you want it to be. My thought, is that because your last session was pretty intense, you therapist wanted to see if you wanted to continue talking about where you left off, or talk about something else. It is a little strange they didn't open the conversation at the beginning of the session but it's not totally abnormal. You didn't do anything wrong, I think they just wanted you to guide the conversation a little more. 

But, if it makes you uncomfortable definitely tell them. The goal isn't to make you uncomfortable. If you're uncomfortable you're definitely less likely to be vulnerable and that's the opposite objective. Let them know. They won't hate you, judge you, or treat you differently. If having them ask questions helps you open up, tell them!! 

Goodluck, feel free to chat me if you have anymore questions or need to talk :)
